research_question: What is the effect of breastfeeding or breast milk compared with no intervention on crying duration in seconds in neonates undergoing a painful procedure?
outcome_description: Duration of crying in seconds during and immediately after a painful procedure
positive_direction: Shorter duration of crying, indicating greater analgesia/comfort favoring breastfeeding over no intervention
search_queries: breastfeeding neonatal procedural pain crying randomized controlled trial
breast milk heel lance venipuncture crying duration neonates trial
breastfeeding pain relief crying time newborn infant controlled experiment
inclusion_criteria: Randomised or quasi-randomised controlled trials evaluating term or preterm neonates (<= 28 days of age) undergoing a painful procedure (e.g., heel lance, venipuncture, injection)
Evaluates direct breastfeeding or expressed breast milk administered during the painful procedure compared against a no-intervention or routine care control arm
Reports quantitative duration of crying during or immediately following the procedure
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, conference abstracts without full data, commentaries, editorials, or study protocols)

No comparison between breastfeeding (direct or expressed milk) and a no-intervention/routine care control group (e.g., active-comparator-only trials comparing breastfeeding to sucrose, glucose, or skin-to-skin alone)
No quantitative outcome data on duration of crying permitting calculation of mean and SD in seconds (e.g., reporting only composite pain scores, physiological parameters, or crying percentage)
Studies conducted in infants older than 28 days of age (non-neonatal populations) or completely unrelated topics
moderators_to_extract: Type of painful procedure (heel lance vs. venipuncture vs. injection)
Intervention delivery mode (direct breastfeeding vs. expressed breast milk)
Gestational age / infant maturity (term vs. preterm neonates)
Control condition specification (routine care vs. no analgesia/comfort measure)
effect_size_note: Pool as mean difference (MD) in seconds. Total crying time during and immediately after the procedure is prioritized over latency to first cry. Minutes converted to seconds (min * 60). Standard errors converted to SD (SE * sqrt(n)). Medians and ranges/IQRs converted to mean and SD using standard estimation methods. Exclude pain scales, physiological markers, and crying percentages.
